title: A later kind's act is priced by its producer even where its module says it still needs something
instrument: a parts-real case: an album composed with no takeId - the words view's write-words act has needs ['a track'], and the real actReceipt for it is refused with the module's words (today: ok, and the confirm launches)
body:
## Summary
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/real.ts receiptFor prices a bound kind's act from the PRODUCER's units only; the kind module's own units refusal (the view's `needs`) is never consulted, so the real side prices and launches an act the editor draws as blocked.

## Description
For a later kind, the view's acts come from the module (e.g. app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureAlbum.ts wordsActs: needs ['a track'] when the project has no take) and the fixture's receipt refuses through module.units. The real receiptFor and launchAct (app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/real.ts) call lib partActReceipt/launchPartAct with the bound producer's UnitsFn only (lib/producers/words.ts wordsUnits prices from the project title and ignores the track). Measured by a throwaway probe: real album-video with no takeId - view write-words needs ['a track'], receipt ok, confirm launched. Fixed: one of the two rules wins on both halves - either receiptFor first runs later(kind).units(ctx, act, target) and refuses with the module's words, or the module's needs drop what the producer does not need. Which rule is right for words (does the mv-metadata turn need the take?) is the call the worker must make from lib/producers/words.ts; the same seam is behind part-port-fixtures' open card 'A trailer's frames view offers a plate render its producer cannot price' (the reverse direction), so one fix should settle both.

## Flow
- compose album-video with no take on the real side
- open /projects/<id>/words: write-words reads 'needs a track'
- actReceipt(write-words) -> ok; act -> launched
- fix: receipt and view read one units rule

## Expected impact
The real editor never prices an act it draws as blocked. Could break: a words dry run that today succeeds without a take.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the view's needs and the receipt agree on the real side
Before: words with no take: needs ['a track'], receipt ok, act launched (probe, deleted)
After: receipt refused with the module's words, or needs [] (predicted)
Method: simulation - which rule is correct lives in lib/producers/words.ts (bound-producers), outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/real.ts receiptFor: partActReceipt(..., bound.value.units, ...)
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureAlbum.ts wordsActs: needs: trackOf(ctx) === null ? ["a track"] : []
lib/producers/words.ts:31 wordsUnits(_s, f, ask) - wordsPlan({ title: f.plan.project.title, ... })

title: Memoize the real scene's research and later-kind records per load
body:
## Summary
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/realScene.ts sceneOf's ctx.research() and ctx.rec(kind) re-map the snapshot on every call; viewOf asks for a verdict per tab and again per upstream part.

## Description
Timed with a throwaway vitest probe (research mapper call count via vi.mock, 10 warm loads per key) over an explainer and a trailer holding the v1 fixture notebook: researchOf runs 7-14 times per loadPart, and a whole loadPart costs 1.3-3.6 ms. Nothing worth a cache and its invalidation.

## Flow
- probe loadPart for research, script, frames, score, cut on two recipes

## Expected impact
None measurable.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - a faster real part view
Before: 1.30-3.58 ms/loadPart, researchOf 7-14 per load
After: not built - nothing to win
Method: probe - timed loop, probe deleted
Result: not-better
Gate: none
evidence: short-educational-video: research 3.31 ms (7 calls), script 2.34 (14), frames 3.58 (14), score 1.55 (7), cut 2.15 (8); trailer: 2.27, 1.67, 1.71, 1.30, 1.87
